key_findings: SEC-43: the agent's own nsec reaches four sinks - McpServer.env (lib.rs:4159-4170) -> session/new (pool.rs:832) -> child stdin (acp.rs:568-571), then unredacted into observe("acp_write") (acp.rs:963) and a debug log on target acp::wire (acp.rs:994). With --relay-observer the frame is NIP-44 encrypted to the owner and stored by the relay as kind 24200; the only transform is 3000-byte elision, which preserves a 63-char nsec.

SEC-44: `buzz --help` prints the live BUZZ_PRIVATE_KEY value to stdout with exit 0 (lib.rs:84-85); hide_env is never set. The ACP harness injects that key into agent subprocesses, so the nsec lands in model transcripts as ordinary success output.

SEC-46/47: buzz-dev-mcp is a self-documented unrestricted execution surface - paths.rs:3-6 'No containment enforcement', four tests assert the absence of a boundary, and shell(command:'env') returns the nsec because shell.rs:171 intentionally inherits it.

SEC-48: buzz-agent's PASSTHROUGH_ENV hands every MCP child NOSTR_PRIVATE_KEY, BUZZ_PRIVATE_KEY, BUZZ_AUTH_TAG, SSH_AUTH_SOCK, GIT_ASKPASS and GIT_SSH_COMMAND (mcp.rs:39-63) while the crate README lists a six-key allowlist and reassures the reader that provider API keys do not leak. env_clear() is correctly used; the gap is the list.

SEC-49: buzz-acp's re-implemented AUTH path regressed the challenge cap from 1-of-3 intake paths to 0-of-3 (relay.rs:3901, :3610-3616, :2344-2348 vs connection.rs:198-201), giving a hostile relay an unbounded sign-and-echo primitive against the agent key.

SEC-50: auto-approve is the shipped posture and undocumented - handle_permission_request returns allow_once for every request (acp.rs:1703-1718) with --permission-mode defaulting to bypass-permissions (config.rs:435).

SEC-54: `buzz patches send --patch-file <any path>` publishes arbitrary file contents as a kind-1617 event body; read_file_or_stdin (validate.rs:195) is unbounded and unconfined, and no CLI file argument uses buzz_persona::safe_resolve, which exists one crate over.

SEC-57: a delegated BUZZ_AUTH_TAG grants full owner authority on every command - the conditions slot (auth tag index 2) is never inspected anywhere in the CLI, so an agent cannot tell locally whether an action is within its delegation.

DEBT-58: ARCHITECTURE.md:658-667's buzz-acp LOC table is wrong on all seven rows; main.rs is listed at 2457 LOC doing 'event loop, pool orchestration' and is actually 3 lines, while lib.rs (6570 lines, where the loop lives) is omitted entirely.

DEBT-59: buzz-acp fully reimplements buzz-ws-client with no dependency on it, down to a byte-identical debug string; the two copies have now diverged in wire coverage (7 inbound message types vs 6, COUNT absent from the acp copy).

DEBT-60: buzz-acp's actual pooling logic has zero tests - 11 functions plus the 948-line run_prompt_task are untested, and tests/pool_lifecycle_state.rs is a 4-line #[path] shim that re-runs the same 9 in-source tests in a second binary.
DEBT-64: nine buzz-agent README claims are materially wrong, including a 16x error on BUZZ_AGENT_MAX_HISTORY_BYTES (documented 1 MiB, actual 16 MiB) and protocolVersion 1 vs 2.

DEBT-73/CFG-2d-13: AGENTS.md documents a `--kinds` flag on `messages search` that does not exist (verified exit 1), and its --format compact example cannot parse. --format itself is silently ignored by 16 of 21 command groups; moderation::dispatch binds it as _format.

DEBT-77/CONV-2d-14: six sites across the batch test a copy of the production rule rather than the rule - notably 3 of 4 BUZZ_ACP_ALLOWED_CHANNEL_ADD_POLICIES tests (admitted in the file's own comment) and the effort-table drift guard, whose most complex branch is dead.

CONV-2d-5: the 1000-line ceiling AGENTS.md documents has no Rust gate; 15 files in this batch exceed it, up to 6570 lines. AGENTS.md states it inside Mobile App section Rules while also saying 'mirroring desktop/web', so its intended scope is genuinely ambiguous.

Zero TODO/FIXME/HACK/XXX markers across buzz-acp, buzz-dev-mcp, buzz-agent's core/LLM/tools groups and all 21 buzz-cli command modules - deferred work is recorded in prose, so no grep-based audit surfaces it. This is why several stale claims in this batch went unnoticed.

Positive: buzz-cli's retry/idempotency layer is the best-engineered code in the batch (kind-aware DeliveryUnknown policy that declines to retry ambiguous moderation writes, 12 behavioural integration tests over live servers); view_image's credential gate is the best-hardened code (scheme+path+host+port match, redirects disabled when a token is attached, magic-byte sniffing, 64 Mpx bomb guard); buzz-cli correctly depends on the shared buzz-ws-client for NIP-42 rather than reimplementing it.
